report.tagline: Booking and payments software for salons, barbers and spas, plus an app where customers find and book them.
report.simpleSummary: Fresha is the system a hair salon or barber uses to run its diary: bookings, reminders, staff rotas and card payments at the till. For years the software was free, and Fresha made money by taking a small cut when customers paid by card. It also runs a marketplace app where people find nearby salons and book online, and Fresha charges the salon a fee for each new customer it brings. Based in London, it now works in about 120 countries.

keyNumbers.label: Valuation
keyNumbers.note: KKR-led $80 million round, May 2026, made Fresha a unicorn. Total funding about $285 million.

keyNumbers.label: Revenue run-rate
keyNumbers.note: Reported May 2026, growing over 60% a year. Fresha says it is profitable.

overview.whatItDoes: Fresha gives beauty and wellness businesses one system for their calendar, client records, online booking, payments, marketing and stock. Customers use the Fresha app or website to find salons, see prices and reviews, and book any time. Fresha earns from card payments, subscription plans introduced in 2025, and a fee on new clients from its marketplace.
howItWorks: A salon signs up, adds its services, prices and staff, and sets opening hours.
Clients book through the salon's own booking link, Instagram, Google, or the Fresha marketplace.
Fresha sends reminders by text and email to cut no-shows, and can take deposits.
At checkout, the salon takes payment with Fresha's card terminal or online, and Fresha keeps a processing fee.
When the Fresha marketplace brings a new client, the salon pays a one-time new client fee.
Salons can pay for subscription plans and add-ons like marketing messages and extra features.
overview.valueProposition: For salons: run the whole business from one easy system without big upfront costs. For customers: find and book a trusted salon any time, in a few taps.

businessModel.summary: Fresha makes money from three things: a cut of card payments, a one-time fee for each new client its marketplace brings, and since 2025, subscription plans and add-ons. The free or cheap software is the hook; payments are the main engine.

revenueStreams.detail: A small percentage plus a fixed fee on each card payment through Fresha Pay.
A share of the first booking when a new client comes from the Fresha marketplace, often around 20%.
Paid plans introduced in 2025, priced per business or per team member.
Marketing messages, advanced features, and financial services.

businessModel.pricing: Subscription plans since 2025, priced per business or per team member (exact prices vary by country). Card processing fees around 1% to 2.5% plus a small fixed fee in the UK. New client fee on marketplace bookings. Prices are estimates from salon reviews and pricing guides.
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a salon that takes £10,000 a month in card payments through Fresha. At about 2% processing, Fresha collects £200, pays maybe £100 to card networks and banks, and keeps about £100. If the marketplace brings 10 new clients a month at £40 each and Fresha keeps 20%, that is another £80. Add a subscription of perhaps £20 to £50. So one busy salon could be worth £200 to £230 a month to Fresha. Small salons are worth much less. These are rough estimates.

growth.moat: Once a salon's diary, client history and card terminals are on Fresha, switching is painful. The marketplace grows stronger as more salons join, because more choice brings more customers, and more customers bring more salons.

pmLessons: You can give software away and make money on payments, because payments grow as your customers' businesses grow.
Changing a free product to paid is risky; explain the value clearly or loyal users feel betrayed.
A marketplace on top of software gives sellers a reason to stay: you bring them customers.
Fees tied to value, like a fee only for new clients, feel fair only if the rules are clear.

interviewQuestions.question: Fresha gave its software away for free. How did it make money?
interviewQuestions.hint: Payments cut, new client fees, add-ons. Explain why payments grow with salon revenue.

interviewQuestions.question: Fresha moved salons to paid plans in 2025. How would you measure if it worked?
interviewQuestions.hint: Revenue per salon, churn, new sign-ups, payment attach. Compare cohorts before and after.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow the consumer marketplace?
interviewQuestions.hint: Supply (salons listed), demand (search, SEO, app), trust (reviews). Pick one lever and a metric.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Fresha's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Appointments completed. Break into active businesses, appointments per business, payment attach, marketplace.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you launch Fresha in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: UPI payments, WhatsApp booking, low prices, competition with local apps like Urban Company for at-home services.
